question: Let $A=\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$ and define a relation $R$ on $A$ by $(x,y)R(u,v)$ if and only if $xv=yu$. Prove that $R$ is an equivalence relation on $A$.
explanation:
Reflexivity
For any $(x,y)\in A$,
$$xy=yx.$$
Therefore, $(x,y)R(x,y)$ for every $(x,y)\in A$. Hence, $R$ is reflexive.

Symmetry
Suppose $(x,y)R(u,v)$. Then
$$xv=yu.$$
Rewriting the equality gives
$$uy=vx.$$
Therefore, $(u,v)R(x,y)$, and hence $R$ is symmetric.

Transitivity
Suppose $(x,y)R(u,v)$ and $(u,v)R(p,q)$. Then
$$xv=yu$$
and
$$uq=vp.$$
Multiplying the first equality by $q$ gives
$$xvq=yuq.$$
Multiplying the second equality by $y$ gives
$$yuq=yvp.$$
Hence,
$$xvq=yvp.$$
Since $v\in\mathbb{N}$ and therefore $v\ne0$, cancelling $v$ gives
$$xq=yp.$$
Thus, $(x,y)R(p,q)$, so $R$ is transitive.

Final Result
The relation $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Therefore, $R$ is an equivalence relation on $A$.

options.A: $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; hence, it is an equivalence relation
options.B: $R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive; hence, it is not an equivalence relation
options.C: $R$ is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive; hence, it is not an equivalence relation
options.D: $R$ is transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric; hence, it is not an equivalence relation
